target_profile.system_boundary: Captured Go raft library. Node serializes raft execution in its run goroutine; RawNode requires caller serialization. Transport, disk durability and application/client completion are caller duties; in-repository MemoryStorage and configuration recovery remain implementation support, not externalized unknown code.
protocol_contexts: Node identity, term/role, log entry term/index, active incoming/outgoing voters, read request context
external_interfaces: Node/RawNode Propose, Step, Tick, Ready, Advance, ApplyConfChange
ownership: raft owns protocol state; caller owns persistent writes, transport and application
variants: AsyncStorageWrites with ordered local append/apply workers
PreVote, CheckQuorum, joint consensus, learners, StepDownOnRemoval

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
activities.realization_summary: Append support is aggregated under active voters and current-term log matching; leader propagates committed prefix.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: Election votes acquire local authority; term, role, lease and quorum checks limit its use.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Stored log and ConfState reconstruct participation; snapshots resynchronize lagging nodes.
Application activates configuration entries; Changer maintains joint/learner eligibility.
Ready or ordered apply messages export committed entries with separate completion bookkeeping.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
activities.realization_summary: Unstable overlay, caller persistence and deferred responses mediate support publication.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
activities.realization_summary: Proposal submission is distinct from committed entry/application completion; ReadIndex uses caller context.

behaviors.execution_owner: Caller serialized RawNode; alternatively node.run goroutine
behaviors.protocol_context: Local node and proposal payload; no committed index yet
implementation_guards: RawNode.Step rejects network local messages and unknown response senders; RawNode itself is thread-unsafe.
external_effects: Propose returns the Step result, not application completion. Ready exposes committed entries separately.
important_branches: Follower forwards only with a known leader and forwarding enabled; candidates drop proposals; node.run disables proposal reception without a leader.
unknowns: Application-specific deduplication and client completion are outside the core library.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current leader term and active progress map; entry index assigned from lastIndex
implementation_guards: Leader must remain in progress map; transfer blocks proposals; size limit can reject; configuration proposals are validated against pending/applied index and joint state.
writes: Entries receive current Term and consecutive Index; appended to unstable log.
external_effects: Broadcast MsgApp with predecessor index/term and commit index; enqueue self MsgAppResp behind persistence.
existing_protections: A new leader appends an empty entry in its term.

behaviors.protocol_context: Message term accepted by Step; leader predecessor index/term and follower committed prefix
implementation_guards: Predecessor term must match unless predecessor is already below committed; conflict with committed prefix panics.
writes: Replace conflicting uncommitted suffix; commit only up to min(message commit,last new index).
external_effects: Queue positive MsgAppResp at accepted last index or existing committed index; rejection includes conflict hint.
existing_protections: Positive response construction is distinct from durable transmission.

behaviors.execution_owner: raft.send, RawNode Ready/acceptReady/Advance and caller storage worker
behaviors.protocol_context: Node term plus queued response and all prior append work
durable_effects: Persistence is caller work, not performed by enqueue or Ready.
external_effects: Synchronous Ready publishes remote responses subject to persistence contract, self responses run on Advance; asynchronous MsgStorageAppend carries all deferred responses.
async_boundaries: Ordered append worker must finish storage before returning attached responses.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Prevents legally published append support from preceding required local persistence.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Election vote replies including self replies are delayed behind storage work.

existing_protections: Responses are deferred for both accepted and rejected votes/appends.
unknowns: Package guide permits same-batch entry persistence parallel with message sending; Ready interface explicitly requires entries first. Applicability requires resolving this difference before using the weaker schedule.

behaviors.execution_owner: Leader stepLeader, ProgressTracker, quorum functions and raftLog.maybeCommit
behaviors.protocol_context: Current term after Step filtering; current voter configuration; per-peer Match
implementation_guards: Unknown progress ignored; old term replies ignored; Match increases only; commit candidate must have current nonzero term.
writes: Update sender Match; compute majority order statistic, minimum across joint majorities; advance committed monotonically.
external_effects: Broadcast commit and release pending read requests on advancing commit.
important_branches: Rejected append responses decrease probe position with stale rejection checks; heartbeat restores flow without supplying append index support.
existing_protections: Learners excluded by voter-set iteration; heartbeat response does not increase Match.

behaviors.protocol_context: Election or pre-election round, term, voter identities, last log identity
behaviors.trigger: Tick timeout, Campaign, vote request/reply or transfer timeout
implementation_guards: Campaign requires promotability and no unapplied committed configuration change.
Vote grant checks vote/leader state and lexicographic last-log freshness; future pre-vote differs from real vote.
Candidate consumes only matching response type; tally considers configured voter IDs and requires both joint majorities.
writes: Real candidacy increments term and records self vote; pre-candidacy resets tally without incrementing term.
external_effects: Queue self vote response for persistence; send vote requests; winning pre-vote starts real campaign; winning real election becomes leader.
existing_protections: Duplicate votes do not overwrite prior tally; lease can suppress a higher-term vote request except forced transfer.

behaviors.protocol_context: Node term, role and pending local work
behaviors.trigger: Higher term message, role change, check-quorum failure or transfer
writes: Term change clears Vote; reset clears tally and remote Match, recreates readOnly, aborts transfer; local Match initializes to lastIndex.
important_branches: Higher pre-vote or granted pre-vote response does not immediately change term.
Lower-term storage append response skips entry stabilization but may apply its snapshot; other obsolete responses are ignored.
Snapshot and committed-application completion are handled separately from election support.
existing_protections: Existing log/committed index survive reset; new leader must satisfy current-term commit check.
unknowns: pendingReadIndexMessages is not cleared by reset; later release re-establishes readOnly tracking under a current-term commit. Detailed request reuse/retry semantics remain open.

behaviors.protocol_context: Applied configuration entry, active incoming/outgoing voter sets and learner sets
implementation_guards: Simple changes cannot change more than one voter or operate in joint state; incoming voter set cannot be emptied.
Joint entry preserves outgoing voters; demotion can stage learner until joint exit.
writes: Retain progress for surviving identities, initialize new identities with Match zero, remove obsolete progress; replace active config.
important_branches: AutoLeave proposal occurs on applied progress under a leader; transfer can delay it.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Active voter sets reinterpret retained Match support; configuration installation can immediately advance commit.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Removal/demotion can step down the leader when configured, prevents promotion as learner and aborts transfer to ineligible target.

unknowns: Full rejection/application duties differ in older package prose and current ApplyConfChange interface.

behaviors.protocol_context: Persisted HardState, ConfState, entries or received snapshot
implementation_guards: Restart bounds stored commit within recovered log; snapshot must exceed commit and include recipient; matching snapshot identity can fast-forward commit without replacement.
writes: Restore term/vote/commit and configuration on restart; enter follower. Snapshot replacement restores committed boundary and configuration.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Recovered commit prefix constrains future append replacement.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Recovery reconstructs eligibility but does not restore leader authority.

unknowns: Disk durability, actual crash recovery and application snapshot installation are caller responsibilities; MemoryStorage is in-memory support only.

behaviors.protocol_context: Committed prefix, applying/applied indices and storage mode
implementation_guards: Outstanding snapshot blocks entry delivery; async mode limits appliable index to stable prefix; application size limit can pause delivery.
writes: Acceptance advances applying; completion moves applied monotonically and releases size accounting.
external_effects: Emit committed entries or MsgStorageApply; application result itself is external.
async_boundaries: Application worker ordered independently from append worker; response Term is zero because committed entries are term-independent.
existing_protections: Node Advance permits pipelined application under ordered Ready application contract; internal applied bookkeeping is not independently observed external application completion.

behaviors.protocol_context: Known per-peer Match and leader commit; follower accepted message term
implementation_guards: Sender caps Commit at min(peer Match,local committed). Receiver Step filters terms.
writes: Follower commitTo is monotone and checks lastIndex.
external_effects: Return heartbeat response, which does not constitute append-index support.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current node term at Ready construction and last entry term/index; ordered append worker
behaviors.trigger: Ready with append work while entries remain unstable or a snapshot needs completion
implementation_guards: needStorageAppendMsg includes changed HardState and deferred responses, not just fresh entries.
needStorageAppendRespMsg includes all unstable entries, including already in-progress entries.
writes: Freeze current node term and last entry identity into MsgStorageAppendResp.
external_effects: Attach the token to MsgStorageAppend.Responses, to be delivered after this and prior ordered append work.

cross_activity_effects.A2: A term-change HardState batch creates a new-term token for an already in-progress suffix, allowing a successor completion after the old token becomes obsolete.

unknowns: A queued token by itself does not prove the caller performed storage work.

behaviors.protocol_context: Delivered local append token, current node term, current unstable overlay
implementation_guards: Step skips entry stabilization and returns on lower token term.
For accepted term, nonzero index passes entry term/index to stableTo; unstable must contain that index as an entry with matching term.
writes: Matching current-context completion removes the acknowledged unstable prefix and advances offset; older-context entry token leaves it alone.
important_branches: Old-term snapshot completion is still passed to appliedSnap, separately from entry stabilization.
Missing entry, snapshot-only identity or mismatching entry term is ignored by unstable.stableTo.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Retaining the unstable overlay prevents eligible log reads from falling back to older in-progress storage contents after an obsolete completion.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Node term and entry term are distinct eligibility coordinates; matching entry identity alone is insufficient across a node-term transition.

existing_protections: raftLog.term checks unstable first; raftLog.slice uses unstable for indices at or above its offset.
unknowns: No same-execution replacement/term-transition schedule has been measured for this lifecycle.

behaviors.protocol_context: ReadOnlySafe, non-singleton active configuration, current-term committed entry, caller request context
behaviors.trigger: Local/forwarded MsgReadIndex or release of a pre-commit pending request
implementation_guards: Without current-term commitment, leader appends request to pendingReadIndexMessages.
For safe mode, addRequest indexes by context bytes and preserves an existing status on repeated context.
writes: Capture current commit index and original request; create empty acknowledgments then self-ack; enqueue context.
unknowns: Same-context retry applicability depends on the version-qualified Node API comment; this question uses distinct contexts.

behaviors.protocol_context: Message term accepted by Step, tracked sender, active voter sets, pending request context
behaviors.trigger: Heartbeat received and subsequent MsgHeartbeatResp delivery
implementation_guards: Follower echoes heartbeat Context.
Leader requires tracked sender, safe mode and nonempty Context; recvAck only updates a currently pending matching context.
Active voter sets must return VoteWon; advance removes status records through the acknowledged queue context.
writes: Record sender in matching request ack map; remove completed queue prefix.
external_effects: responseToReadIndexReq emits original request context and captured index, either local ReadState or remote MsgReadIndexResp.

cross_activity_effects.A7: ReadState gives a request-specific application barrier, not a completed state-machine read.

existing_protections: Old-term heartbeat responses are filtered by Step; reset recreates readOnly with no acknowledgment state.

behaviors.protocol_context: StateLeader and tracker.IsSingleton(), which checks cardinality but not local identity
behaviors.trigger: ReadIndex on a node still in leader state
implementation_guards: IsSingleton checks one incoming voter and empty outgoing configuration.
Unlike MsgProp, the shortcut does not require local progress membership.
external_effects: responseToReadIndexReq immediately emits local committed index and request context without heartbeat confirmation.

cross_activity_effects.A2: When StepDownOnRemoval is false, removed leader role may survive even though sole eligible voter is another node.
cross_activity_effects.A7: The shortcut exports a ReadState barrier; a client result is not observed by this behavior.

unknowns: Compatibility of retained leader role after local removal with safe-read output needs a scoped interface check.

facts.recovery: Reconstructed through stored log/HardState/ConfState where applicable; volatile role and support are reset.

facts.durability: Volatile library assertion; persistence or external completion requires the caller contract, unless explicitly stated.
facts.recovery: Reconstructed through stored log/HardState/ConfState where applicable; volatile role and support are reset.

facts.meaning: The local committed index advanced through current-term quorum aggregation, accepted leader commit bounded by matched append, heartbeat commit, or snapshot/recovery. These producers have different preconditions; commit does not itself mean application completed.
facts.validity_context: Local log prefix preserved across role changes
facts.durability: Volatile library assertion; persistence or external completion requires the caller contract, unless explicitly stated.
facts.recovery: Reconstructed through stored log/HardState/ConfState where applicable; volatile role and support are reset.
unknowns: Global agreement requires relating legal producer histories, not equating commit variables in isolation.

facts.meaning: The library constructed a local append completion token identifying its creation node term and a selected last entry term/index. Delivery under the async caller contract means ordered work through its enclosing batch completed; the token alone does not establish that its entry identity is still eligible to release the current unstable overlay.
facts.validity_context: Conditional on actual ordered storage completion and consumer checks against current node term and unstable entry identity.
facts.durability: The token is volatile; durable completion is a caller obligation before delivery.
facts.recovery: Not recovered as a token. Startup reconstructs log from Storage; a term-change HardState Ready can issue a successor token for remaining unstable entries.
unknowns: Physical persistence and arbitrary crashes are outside this source explanation.

facts.meaning: The leader registered a pending safe-read context with a captured committed index, original request and self acknowledgment; later follower acknowledgments are attached only through that context lookup. Registration alone is not quorum confirmation or a completed read.
facts.validity_context: ReadOnlySafe pending map in current leader context, under caller request-context duties and current active voter set.
facts.durability: Volatile; not part of HardState or log persistence.
facts.recovery: No recovery of acknowledgment map; caller retries when a read request is lost.
unknowns: Context reuse across separate invocations is not authorized by the selected distinct-context scope.

surfaces.entry_point: doc.go usage step 2 versus node.go Ready.Messages
surfaces.reason: The package usage text permits messages while same-batch entries persist; Ready requires sending after Entries persist. This is a concrete contract ambiguity affecting the legality of a delayed-storage schedule, not an established violation.

Pending pre-commit reads survive reset while heartbeat acknowledgment state is replaced. Fresh current-term release is a protection; precise retry/context and invocation responsibility remain to be investigated.
Disk persistence and externally visible application/client effects are application duties. In-repository MemoryStorage is support and is not evidence of disk durability.

Old node-term entry completions are rejected before entry identity matching. A changed HardState can issue a current-term successor token for in-progress entries; snapshot completion is a separate branch.
Distinct request contexts avoid the version-qualified retry ambiguity. A retained prior heartbeat response can be produced and replayed through the public API to test request-support correlation.

formation.explanation: A serialized RawNode.Propose (or node.run proposal event) enters raft.Step. A follower forwards to a known leader or drops; a candidate drops. A leader rejects transfer/removal/quota cases, assigns term/index, appends locally and broadcasts predecessor-qualified MsgApp. Followers check predecessor and committed-prefix conflicts, append only conflicting suffixes, bound advertised commit, and queue replies. Both follower replies and leader self-acks pass through msgsAfterAppend; legal publication relies on caller persistence, directly via Ready/Advance or ordered async append Responses. The leader term-filters replies and raises sender Match. Tracker considers only active voters, majority order statistics and both halves of joint configuration. raftLog.maybeCommit additionally requires the candidate entry to match the current term. Commit propagates via append or Match-capped heartbeat. Ready exports committed entries; async apply waits for local stability. Application and public client completion remain separate caller actions; proposal acceptance does not promise commitment.

context.explanation: Ticks or Campaign trigger hup only when promotable and without unapplied committed configuration changes. PreVote can gather prospective support without increasing term; real candidacy resets state, increments term and records self vote. Self and remote vote replies are queued behind persistence. Vote grants require vote/leader eligibility and last-log freshness. Matching response type and active voter quorum determine victory; the new leader resets progress and appends its current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages normally force follower transition, with lease/pre-vote exceptions; obsolete responses are rejected. CheckQuorum can cause same-term stepdown. Transfer pauses proposals, catches the target up and sends TimeoutNow; timeout or ineligibility aborts transfer. Restart restores HardState/log/configuration and starts as follower. Configuration entries activate through ApplyConfChange, changing voters and optionally causing removal stepdown.

connection.explanation: Term/role reset clears election tally, remote replication support and readOnly acknowledgments, while preserving log and committed prefix; current-term matching prevents a fresh leader from advancing commitment solely using an old-term candidate index. Queued/in-flight responses may outlive resets, so Step term checks remain necessary. StorageAppendResp carries both creation term and entry identity: old-term entry stabilization is skipped even if entry term/index recur, but committed snapshot application survives that term change. StorageApplyResp is term-zero and represents committed work independent of leadership. Configuration changes retain existing participant progress but change which IDs count; switching configuration can immediately rerun commitment. Snapshots recover configuration as well as log boundary. Safe reads wait for current-term commitment (except singleton shortcut), track context-specific heartbeat acknowledgments under active voters, then expose read index to a caller that still must wait for application. reset replaces readOnly but does not clear pendingReadIndexMessages; release retries them only after a current-term commit, creating fresh acknowledgment tracking.

open_details: Resolve doc.go same-batch persistence concurrency versus Ready.Messages entries-before-send interface before testing that weaker schedule.
Read-only lease assumptions, retry context reuse and survival of pending reads across multiple terms need focused applicability review.
MemoryStorage compaction/error paths, detailed bootstrap and all flow-control failure variants are not exhaustively mapped.
An internal Advance/applied update is not proof that external application or client return completed.
core_overview.rationale: The representative proposal, vote/term transition and old-work paths have been followed through actual quorum, log, storage-message and membership callees. This is a source-grounded backbone for selecting questions, not a correctness judgment or exhaustive coverage.
